ai.literal: She who possesses virtues fitting for the home, and who lives within the resources of her husband who married her, is the companion of life.
ai.translation: She who possesses the virtues fitting for a home and lives within the means of her husband is the true partner in life.
ai.modern: இல்லறத்திற்கு ஏற்ற நற்பண்புகளை உடையவளாகி, தன்னை மணந்த கணவனுடைய வருவாய்க்கு ஏற்ப வாழ்பவளே வாழ்க்கைத் துணை ஆவாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential qualities of an ideal life partner. First, she must possess the noble virtues that are fitting for running a household smoothly. Second, she must manage domestic life wisely, keeping expenses in proportion to her husband's financial resources. A woman who combines domestic excellence with financial prudence is celebrated as the true companion of life.

ai.literal: If household excellence is absent in the wife, domestic life, of whatever other excellence it may be, is nothing.
ai.translation: If a wife lacks the virtues that dignify a home, domestic life is nothing, no matter what other greatness it may possess.
ai.modern: மனைவியிடம் இல்லறத்திற்குரிய நற்பண்புகள் இல்லையென்றால், அந்த வாழ்க்கை எவ்வளவு பெருமைகளை உடையதாக இருந்தாலும் ஒரு பயனும் இல்லாததாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights that the true value of a home depends entirely on the wife's character. The term 'manaimāṭci' refers to the virtues and qualities necessary for running a household. If the wife ('illāḷ') lacks these qualities, the poet asserts that the domestic life ('vāḻkkai') is empty or non-existent ('il'). This remains true regardless of whatever other wealth, status, or greatness ('eṉaimāṭcittu āyiṉum') the family might possess.

ai.literal: What is lacking, if the wife is excellent? What is present, if the wife lacks excellence?
ai.translation: What is lacking if the wife possesses noble virtues? And what is truly possessed if she lacks them?
ai.modern: மனைவி நற்பண்புகள் உடையவளாக இருந்தால் அங்கே இல்லாதது என்று எதுவுமில்லை; அவள் நற்பண்புகள் இல்லாதவளாக இருந்தால் அங்கே இருப்பது என்று எதுவுமில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that a wife's character is the true wealth of a household. If a wife possesses noble virtues (மாண்பு), the home lacks nothing, even in the absence of material riches. Conversely, if she lacks these qualities (மாணாக்கடை), no amount of material wealth can bring genuine prosperity or fulfillment. The poet uses a powerful rhetorical structure, contrasting 'what is lacking' with 'what is present', to show that domestic happiness depends entirely on the wife's goodness.

ai.literal: Than a woman, what things of greater worth are there, if the firmness called fidelity is present?
ai.translation: What is of greater worth than a woman, if she possesses the firm strength of character called fidelity?
ai.modern: கற்பு என்று சொல்லப்படும் மனஉறுதி ஒரு பெண்ணிடம் இருக்குமானால், அவளை விடப் பெருமைக்குரியவை வேறு என்ன இருக்கின்றன?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of a wife's moral integrity and strength of character. The poet uses the word 'திண்மை', which means firmness or unshakeable strength, to define 'கற்பு' (fidelity), showing it is an active power rather than a passive state. If a woman possesses this inner strength, there is absolutely nothing of greater worth or dignity in life than her.

ai.literal: Deity not-worshipping, husband having-worshipped she-who-rises, 'pour' upon-saying, will-pour rain.
ai.translation: If a wife who does not worship any other deity rises worshipping her husband, the rain will pour down at her command.
ai.modern: தெய்வத்தை வணங்காமல், தன் கணவனையே வணங்கித் துயில் எழுகின்ற பெண், 'மழை பெய்' என்று சொன்னால் உடனே மழை பெய்யும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the immense power of a wife's devotion and moral strength. The poet states that a woman who does not worship any external deity, but instead rises each day worshipping her husband, possesses such spiritual power that even nature obeys her. If she commands the rain to fall, it will immediately pour down. The key words 'தொழாஅள்' (she who does not worship other gods) and 'தொழுதெழுவாள்' (she who rises worshipping her husband) contrast the redirection of her devotion, while 'பெய்யெனப் பெய்யும்' (will pour as soon as told to pour) illustrates the absolute authority her virtue commands over the elements.

ai.literal: Protecting herself, cherishing her husband, preserving the highly excellent reputation, and being without negligence, is a wife.
ai.translation: She who guards her own virtue, cherishes her husband, preserves the excellent reputation of the family, and remains unwearied in her duties, is a true wife.
ai.modern: தன்னைக் காத்துக்கொண்டு, தன்னை மணந்த கணவனைப் பேணி, தகுதியமைந்த புகழைக் காத்து, கடமைகளில் சோர்வில்லாமல் விளங்குபவளே சிறந்த பெண் ஆவாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the core virtues of an ideal wife. First, she protects her own character and virtue. Second, she cares for and supports her husband who took her in marriage. Third, she preserves the excellent reputation of their household. Finally, she performs all these duties without any negligence or weariness. A woman who embodies these qualities is celebrated as a true life-partner.

ai.literal: What will physical confinement guarding do? For women, the guard of guarding self-restraint indeed is foremost.
ai.translation: Of what use is physical confinement to guard women? The self-restraint with which they guard themselves is the foremost protection.
ai.modern: பெண்களைச் சிறைவைத்துத் தடுக்கும் காவல் என்ன பயனைச் செய்யும்? அவர்கள் தங்களது நிறை என்னும் சுயக்கட்டுப்பாட்டால் தங்களைக் காத்துக் கொள்ளும் காவலே முதன்மையானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts external physical restraint with internal moral strength. The poet asks what benefit can possibly come from locking women up or guarding them physically. Instead, the self-restraint and moral integrity, referred to as 'niṟai', which women possess to guard themselves, is declared to be the ultimate and most effective protection. True virtue cannot be forced from the outside; it must come from within.

ai.literal: If they obtain a worthy husband, and if they act accordingly, wives will attain great glory in the world where the gods dwell.
ai.translation: If wives obtain a worthy husband and live in true devotion to him, they will win great glory in the world where the gods dwell.
ai.modern: பெண்கள் தகுதியான கணவனைப் பெற்று, அவனுக்கு ஏற்றவாறு அன்போடு வாழ்ந்தால், தேவர்கள் வாழும் மேலுலகத்தில் பெரும் சிறப்பினை அடைவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the ultimate spiritual reward of a devoted wife. The word 'பெற்றால்' refers to obtaining a virtuous husband, while 'பெறின்' means living in a manner that honors and cherishes that relationship. If a woman achieves this harmonious domestic life, she is promised 'பெருஞ்சிறப்பு' (great glory) in 'புத்தேளிர் வாழும் உலகு' (the world where celestial beings dwell). The poet suggests that the quiet virtues of a dedicated household life elevate a woman to a status celebrated even in the divine realms.

ai.literal: To those who do not have a wife who cherishes fame, there is no majestic walk like a bull before those who despise them.
ai.translation: Those who do not have a wife who cherishes a good reputation cannot walk with the majestic stride of a bull in front of their detractors.
ai.modern: புகழை விரும்பும் மனைவியைப் பெறாதவர்களுக்கு, தம்மை இகழ்ந்து பேசுபவர் முன்னால் காளையைப் போலப் பெருமிதத்தோடு நடக்கும் கம்பீர நடை இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the social standing a virtuous wife brings to her husband. The word 'இல்' (literally home) here represents the wife who is the soul of the household. If she does not cherish and protect the family's reputation ('புகழ்புரிந்த'), the husband loses his honor in society. Without this domestic strength, he cannot face his mockers ('இகழ்வார்') with confidence, losing the proud, majestic stride ('பீடு நடை') compared here to that of a strong bull ('ஏறு').

ai.literal: Auspiciousness, they say, is the excellence of the household; and its good ornament is the obtaining of good children.
ai.translation: They say the true auspiciousness of a home is the excellence of the wife; and its finest ornament is the blessing of good children.
ai.modern: இல்லறத்தின் நற்பண்பே அதன் மங்கலம் என்று கூறுவர்; அந்த இல்லறத்திற்கு நல்ல அணிகலன் நல்ல பிள்ளைகளைப் பெறுவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true wealth and beauty of a domestic life. The poet states that the inherent virtue and excellence of the wife (மனைமாட்சி) constitutes the true auspiciousness (மங்கலம்) of a home. Furthermore, the ultimate ornament (நன்கலம்) that beautifies this household is the blessing of raising virtuous children (நன்மக்கட்பேறு). By comparing children to jewels, the couplet emphasizes that moral excellence and family harmony are far superior to material wealth.
